items.name: Promote Scoutbook Signups
items.description: Promote Scoutbook signups by published deadline at troop meetings and via email to troop.

items.name: Promote Event Creatively
items.description: Be creative! Share photos from past events (connect a laptop to the TV during troop meetings), give precise information about where/when/what it is, and tell scouts why your event is going to be great!

items.name: Discuss Event Plan at PLC Meetings
items.description: Make sure everyone is informed about: Where (locations), When (dates), What (logistics - equipment, foods), and How (transportation).

items.name: Promote Scoutbook Signups
items.description: Promote Scoutbook signups by published deadline at troop meetings and via email to troop.

items.name: Develop Event Schedule
items.description: Develop an event schedule and share it with the Adult-in-Charge (AIC).

items.name: Review Patrol Participation and Combine Patrols
items.description: For outings that include tenting and/or cooking, review patrol participation and combine scouts from under-represented patrols with other patrols; if PLs/APLs are not in attendance, appoint PLs as needed for outing patrols.

items.name: Schedule Pack Check
items.description: Schedule a pack check for backpacking and high adventure trips.

items.name: Check Patrol Readiness with PLs
items.description: Check with PLs to ensure tenting and cooking plans are in place, patrol box is ready (clean, complete, location/carrier known), and Grubmasters are purchasing food as needed.

items.name: Create Car Travel Seating Arrangements
items.description: Create seating arrangements for car travel to/from event in coordination with the AIC.

items.name: Share Event Schedule with PLs
items.description: Share the event schedule with the PLs.

items.name: Check Attendance
items.description: Check that the scouts who RSVP'd yes are present (if not, try to contact them).

items.name: Collect Required Forms and Information
items.description: Check with AIC on forms. Medical forms A, B1, B2 are required for all outings; Medical form C (signed by doctor) is required for 72+ hour outings; Aquatics participation requires scouts to be certified swimmers.

items.name: Verify Patrol Gear and Patrol Boxes
items.description: Check that PLs have all their gear, including their patrol box.

items.name: Check Stove Fuel Supply
items.description: Check that each PL has enough fuel, if stoves will be used on the outing.

items.name: Monitor Headcounts and Buddy System
items.description: Monitor scouts headcounts, help enforce the buddy system, and ensure scouts live up to troop motto (Nobody Walks Alone).

items.name: Direct Formations and Campsite Setup
items.description: Direct pack lines, fall ins, campsite selection, loading and unloading.

items.name: Organize Activities and Perform Safety Checks
items.description: Organize activities as called for by event plan and perform safety checks as needed.

items.name: Encourage Photos and Monitor Cell Phone Usage
items.description: Encourage scouts to take pictures and monitor cell phone usage to ensure it conforms with troop cell phone policy.

items.name: Maintain Leave No Trace Standard
items.description: Clean up & sweep campsites.

items.name: Lead Campfire and Closing
items.description: MC campfire as appropriate and close the outing with Roses, Buds, and Thorns.

items.name: Assign Equipment Cleaning
items.description: Ensure PLs have assigned patrol QMs or participating scouts to take home all used equipment for cleaning to be ready by next troop meeting.

items.name: Collect and Share Event Photos
items.description: Encourage scouts to upload photos to the troop shared drive, and check with Social Media Chair and Historian to share photo updates for social media/website.

items.name: Provide Feedback to PLC
items.description: Present written feedback to PLC and lead discussion of any learning.

items.name: Review Highlights at Next Troop Meeting
items.description: At next troop meeting: describe outing highlights and then have participants say what they liked most about the outing.
